_about: Terms taught in one course and used in a later one. In lesson text, write program (data-term can be left out when the words are the term itself). The word gets a dotted underline; hovering or tapping it opens a bubble with 'says' (one plain-English sentence, using only words the course that taught it had taught), 'ex' (an example) and a link to the lesson that taught it. 'course' is an id in curriculum.json; 'lesson' is a lesson or panel id in that course; 'name' is how that lesson is labelled there. Every guide reads this one list, so a term is always explained the same way (docs/pedagogy.md, rule 16).

program.says: A program is a list of instructions the computer follows. Each command you type runs a program.
program.ex: ls and cat are programs. So is your web browser.
program.name: Backstage

file.says: A file holds one thing on a computer, like some writing or a picture. Files live in folders.
file.name: Look around

file name.says: The name a file is saved under. Every letter counts, and capitals matter.
file name.name: Look around
